title: Methodus nova et facilis calculum variationum tractandi

deep.reconstruction:
Context (§§9-11): Euler studies the integral J[y] = ∫Z dx, where Z = Z(x, y, p, q, r, …) with p = y', q = y'', r = y''', and dZ = M dx + N dy + P dp + Q dq + R dr + …. He embeds the curve in a one-parameter family y(x,t), with t = 0 the original curve. The variation of J is then the first-order change dt·(∂/∂t)∫Z dx at t = 0. Because x is not varied, the M-term drops out, and Z changes by dt(N y_t + P y_{xt} + Q y_{xxt} + R y_{xxxt} + …).

On this page Euler splits the variation into separate integrals:
δJ = dt∫N dx (∂y/∂t) + dt∫P dx (∂²y/∂x∂t) + dt∫Q dx (∂³y/∂x²∂t) + dt∫R dx (∂⁴y/∂x³∂t) + …

He then remarks that if both y(x) and the family y(x,t) were given explicitly, all the mixed partials could be evaluated, t set to 0, and the integrals computed directly. This is the 'determinate' case.

§12: in maxima/minima problems the relation between x and y is unknown. It is to be found from the condition that δJ = 0 however the parameter t is introduced, i.e. for an arbitrary variation η = ∂y/∂t. The quantities y_t, y_{xt}, y_{xxt}, … then have no fixed values.

§13 (continued on the next page) announces the 'singular artifice': integrate by parts repeatedly so that every term contains only η = ∂y/∂t. Boundary terms are left over, and the integrand becomes (N − P' + Q'' − R''' + …)η. Setting this to zero gives the Euler–Lagrange equation.

In modern terms, the page sets up the first variation as the derivative along a one-parameter family (a Gateaux derivative). It also motivates why arbitrary variations force the coefficient of η to vanish.

ideas.what: Variation of ∫Z dx defined as the t-derivative along a one-parameter family y(x,t) at t=0, written as a sum of integrals of mixed partials
ideas.modern_name: First variation as a directional (Gateaux) derivative along a family of comparison curves
ideas.where_published: E420 itself (Novi Comm. Petrop. 16); see also the 3rd supplement to Institutiones calculi integralis vol. 3 (E385-related)

ideas.what: Distinction between a determinate problem (given y and given family, so the integral can be computed outright) and an extremal problem (y unknown, variation must vanish for every admissible family)
ideas.modern_name: Arbitrariness of the variation η, the premise of the fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler/Lagrange; the lemma was made rigorous later (Du Bois-Reymond, 19th c.)

ideas.what: Announcement of integration by parts to reduce all terms to the form ∫(…)·∂y/∂t dx
ideas.modern_name: Derivation of the Euler–Lagrange equation for higher-order Lagrangians, with boundary terms
ideas.where_published: E65, E296, E420, Opera omnia I.25

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard, well-known expository step in Euler's famous 'new method' paper. The parameter-t formulation of the variation is documented in the Opera omnia I.25 commentary (Carathéodory) and in Goldstine's history. Nothing on this page appears unrecorded.
